evidence.note: Real boto3 round-trips for core CRUD and deliberate wrong-credential SigV4 probes (SignatureDoesNotMatch vs InvalidAccessKeyId), catching real breakage — well beyond ad hoc pokes.
boto3 edge-case verification: multipart complete with ETag format check, versioning, tagging, CopyObject, multi-object delete — systematic per-operation exercising.

Admin API and console API tested directly via curl; presigned GET/PUT, ranged 206, invalid range 416, conditional 304, cross-tenant 403 all confirmed with boto3/HTTP — hits multiple grader conditions.
Console verified only by static grep of data-testids in app.js and 200-status static file loads; no browser DOM/side-effect verification.

Concurrency (30-client), lifecycle fast-clock expiry, notification webhook delivery/retry, UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, and audit atomicity were named as 'still need to verify' but never actually executed before submit — subsystems left unverified.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it used real boto3 to exercise not just main operations but many edge cases (multipart ETag, ranged 206/416, conditional 304, cross-tenant status codes) and hit admin/console APIs directly, using failures to drive fixes. But it falls short of level 8 because two of that anchor's three pillars are missing: no concurrency stress test for the explicit 30-client requirement (only lock code was added), and console verification was a static testid grep rather than browser side-effect checks. Lifecycle, notification, UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, and audit-atomicity were acknowledged but never run, so no reusable regression harness exists — placing it solidly between 5 and 8.
